text: 🌟🌟🌟 THE BEST TOY IN THE WORLD!!! Today only!!!
explanation: "Best in the world" is an opinion — nobody can prove that. And "today only" tries to rush you into buying fast.
This is a fact: you can grab a ruler and check the measurement.

text: You'll love this MORE than anything you've ever tried!
explanation: Nobody knows what you'll feel. It's an exaggerated opinion meant to excite you.

text: This flashlight uses two AA batteries.
explanation: This is a fact you can check by opening the flashlight.

text: Last units left! Buy NOW before it's gone!
explanation: Creating urgency ("last units", "now") is an advertising technique to make you decide without thinking.
It's a fact: you can weigh the bar on a scale.

text: The number 1 flavor chosen by ALL kids!
explanation: "All kids" is an exaggeration — it's impossible to ask every child in the world.
It's a simple fact that anyone can see and confirm.

text: FREE if you buy now! Don't miss this one-time chance!
explanation: "Free" next to "buy now" is a technique to make you decide fast, without really thinking if you need it.
This is a fact: you can open the box and count the crayons.

text: Be the envy of all your friends with this AMAZING toy!
explanation: Promising you'll be "the envy of everyone" is an exaggerated opinion meant to make you want it by comparing yourself to others.

text: This toy box measures 30 by 20 centimeters.
explanation: This is a fact you can confirm with a measuring tape.

text: Approved by the world's greatest champions!
explanation: Saying it's "approved by champions" without proof is a technique to make it seem more trustworthy than it really is.
This is a simple fact: just count the balloons in the pack.

text: You won't believe what this toy does! Watch NOW!!!
explanation: Phrases like "you won't believe" create exaggerated curiosity to keep you watching, even without saying anything concrete.

text: This toy car has four wheels.
explanation: This is a simple fact that anyone can see and confirm.
